To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
a semantic tagger can be constructed for English, based on the LDOCE, if it is combined with a reliable and efficient lemmatizer.

1) a semantic tagging for English should attach to each token a set of semantic attributes or features rather than one single sem-tag; 2) the features should include a meaning definition in terms of a Defining Vocabulary; 3) this meaning definition should be processed to remove stop-list words and repetitions; 4) a semantic tagger can be derived from a large English dictionary, combined with a robust English lemmatiser.

- a domain-independent semantic tagging of English corpora is feasible, and that such a semantic tagging should be based on a restricted Defining vocabulary and selectional restrictions; and - a semantic tagging of English text is not only useful, but also a prerequisite for the study of lexical meaning and meaning associations in English corpora.
In summary, our research is concerned with
developing a domain-independent semantic tagging scheme for English, and a method for automatically applying this scheme to a large corpus of English text.
the development of an automated semantic tagger for use in the study of the meaning associations of English words, and in particular with the study of semantic fields.

a semantic tagger for a large English corpus should: 1. be domain-independent; 2. use the Longman Dictionary as the Defining Vocabulary; 3. use the Longmandictionary to derive semantic features for each lexical item; 4. use a robust lemmatizer, such as the one described by Church et al., to group together inflected andderived forms of the same item, and thus to derive a lemma for each lexical item.
(1) semantic tagging is a valuable tool for the study of the semantics of English text, and that (2) a domain-independent semantic tagging of large corpora is feasible.
the LDC is the most suitable dictionary for semantic tagging, if it can be combined with a robust and accurate lemmatiser, which is not yet available.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
a semantic tagger is not only possible, but is also a practical tool for corpus linguists.

we can now automatically annotate large corpora with semantic features which are useful for many linguistic and computational applications, and that we have developed a new method of corpus annotation which is more useful than Part-of-Speech annotation for many linguistic applications.
we have shown the feasibility of a robust semantic tagger, and that it has a number of applications, both in corpus linguistics and elsewhere.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the LDOCE, with its Defining Vocabulary, is a valuable resource for semantic analysis of English corpora, and can be used as the basis for a domain-independent semantic tagging scheme for English.
a domain-independent English semantic tagger can be built, and is useful for the study of semantic associations in large corpora, and for the study of lexical semantics more generally.
semantic tagging of large corpora, using a restricted Defining vocabulary, is feasible.
